reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 discusses DSC on small organic molecules, not HEAs. E2 mentions HEAs only in passing regarding mixing entropy and melting point depression, without validating DSC or CALPHAD for property extraction. E3 describes general heat capacity behavior and configurational entropy but provides no experimental validation of the proposed method. No evidence supports the claimed accuracy or the specific application of lever-rule and CALPHAD to HEAs.
premises: DSC can accurately measure melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy for HEAs
Lever-rule analysis of DSC traces enables phase fraction deconvolution at melting
CALPHAD modeling provides reliable predictions of HEA thermodynamic properties
Configurational entropy stabilizes single-phase HEA and governs melting signatures
The combined DSC+CALPHAD approach achieves 5–10% accuracy vs. independent techniques
